newsitem.title: USA: Edison seeks amendment of LADWP partner bid.
newsitem.headline: Edison seeks amendment of LADWP partner bid.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council is expected to decide Wednesday on a motion directing the city's municipal electric utility to re-open bidding for a strategic business partner.
"We want to be considered fairly" as a potential partner, said Tom Higgins, a spokesman for Edison International's Southern California Edison Co.
The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) last year began a selection process for a power marketing partner to help the municipal utility enter the era of deregulation.
LADWP still plans to select a partner--out of finalists Enron Corp, PacifiCorp and Duke/Louis Dreyfus--at its board meeting on Tuesday, said Karen Denne, a spokeswoman for LADWP.
The board of the LADWP said last week it would consider Edison, along with other California utilities such as Southern California Gas Co, as potential partners for the regulated side of its business.
But Edison has lobbied heavily for an amendment of the selection process following its decision late last year to sell-off all of its fossil-fueled power plants.
The utility argues that it should be eligible to assist with LADWP's unregulated as well as regulated businesses now that it will not be considered a net generator of power.
"Instead of piecemealing the process it ought to be done in a comprehensive fashion," Higgins at Edison said.
"We have got the ability to generate the greatest savings for DWP," he added.
The motion before the L.A. council calls for extending the process of selecting a strategic partner by 30 days.
